subject: nineTailedKitsune
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: nine-tailed kitsune fox with spirit flames.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I'm planning the full fox model carefully to fit in one response — a four-legged fox facing forward with nine fanned tails ending in glowing spirit flames, a separate jaw, ears, eyes, and kumadori-style red and gold markings.

Now I'm working out the skeleton: a hips root joint feeding a spine chain through chest and neck up to the head, then building the body shape as a swept surface along that spine path to keep the geometry efficient.

For coloring I'm going with a kitsune cream-white coat using countershading, with the neck tapering slightly via its own sweep. For the head, I'm adding a sphere-based skull plus a snout cone, with a separate jaw joint for the lower jaw part.

Still building snout and jaw capsules...

I'm shaping the ears as extruded triangular outlines with sharp tips, positioned on either side of the head with a red inner ear layer offset slightly forward. For eyes, I'm considering decals placed on the front sides of the skull sphere, though I'm wary decals might be unreliable here.

Deciding to use simple plane geometry for eyes instead, calculating the proper surface depth using the sphere equation so the planes sit flush against the skull at the right offset, then adding a slit-shaped gold eye texture with mirroring for left/right sides. Moving on to legs now, setting up the front leg roots and feet positions with appropriate lengths for the limb rig.

Naming the leg joints now—front legs as shoulder/elbow/hand, hind legs as hip/knee/hock/foot, with "L" suffix for the left side, parented to the spine and hips respectively. I'm assigning leg thickness sweeps and a dark gradient color for the fur, giving the kitsune darker "sock" legs.

Next I'm planning the nine tails, rooted at the rump and parented to the hips, fanned out in a 160-degree arc with each tail's azimuth offset by 17 degrees and curved upward using catmull paths.

Working out tail naming to keep joint names unique across indices, then defining a radius function that bulges near the base and tapers toward the tip for the tail segments.

Now I'm planning the color gradient, running cream near the base into a fiery tip, with a cooler blue-violet accent toward the very end, and adding a glowing flame card at the tail tip for a spirit-fire effect.

For the tails I'll use a gradient from white to violet per tail. Then I'm adding floating spirit orbs—hitodama style with glowing spheres and flame cards above—scattered around the fox at varying heights, plus forehead and cheek markings via decals.

For the eyes I'm adding a red streak texture extending outward from each one, mirrored for symmetry. Then I'm working out a rope collar looped around the neck with a shimenawa-style sweep, though I'll likely skip the paper shide details to keep things simple.

Now I'm placing a gold bell sphere at the front of the neck, carefully positioning the collar loop around a neck joint so it doesn't intersect the body sweep, targeting the neck surface specifically. I'm also planning spiky cheek ruffs in white with red tips alongside a chest mane.

Writing zigzag outline points...

Now I'm considering a thin red sweep along the spine line for a ridge marking, trusting the sweep tool to follow the body's bone chain despite the risk of knots at bone cuts. Then I'm planning a gold forehead decal, sketching a flame-like teardrop shape for it.

I'm also adding decals for shoulder swirls on each flank, projecting red/gold SVG patterns onto the body surface, and weighing whether to include gold leg rings or tail-base bands. Finally I'm cataloging the texture set I'll need—eye, mark, swirl, flame in blue and violet—before moving on to sketch the eye SVG itself.

Writing eye and flame SVG shapes...

Continuing the chain: neck connects from chest to head with two joints, then head joint positioned above with its own skull sphere dimensions.

Now I'm defining the muzzle as a tapered capsule extending forward from the head, the jaw as a separate joint with its own bone and capsule, and starting on a small nose sphere positioned at the muzzle tip.

Still placing ear geometry and colors...

Now for the tail flames, I'm setting up frames anchored at the tail tip joint, using card geometry sized roughly 0.2 by 0.36 with cross-flow enabled for a flame-like effect.

Next I'm placing five glowing orbs with a light blue tint, each paired with a flame card frame positioned slightly above, rigged loosely to the nearest joint. I'm debating whether to add a glowing rune mark on the forehead using a decal, but worried the decal material might not support glow properly.

Moving on to the bell and collar geometry, then working out foot placement for ground contact—sizing small foot spheres so their bottoms sit right at y=0, and adjusting leg bend lengths so the front legs reach from shoulder to foot without overstretching.

Now I'm setting up the hind leg chain similarly, checking bend distances fit within joint lengths, and naming chains by side (L/R) with parent joints tied to the spine. I'm sweeping thickness profiles along each chain to build the leg geometry.

Then I'm defining the color scheme: a countershaded cream-tan coat with dark purple sock gradients on the legs, and considering subtle warm tinges on the body. For the tail, I'm setting up a gradient paint that transitions from coat color to a tip color along the tail's curve path.

I'm also working out the geometry—calculating where each tail attaches at the base, how far it extends, and the curvature points that shape its sweep using trig based on the tail's angle.

Now I'm setting up the imports from the SDK builder—things like the catmull curve helper, limb and countershading utilities, and glow effects—to construct the creature's parts, then starting on the flame SVG asset.

Now I'm working out a violet color variant and positioning a swirl decal on the body's flank, figuring out the sweep placement and mirroring logic for the surface detail.
